memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone could count the dust, then your offspring could be counted." - Gen 13:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God makes a staggering promise to a man with no children at all. "Your offspring will be like the dust of the earth" - beyond counting, beyond imagining. Remember, Sarai was barren (Gen 11:30), and Abram was nearly eighty. He had zero descendants. And God speaks of dust that cannot be numbered.

This is how God delights to work. He makes promises that are impossible on human terms, so that when they come to pass, no one can claim credit but Him. If Abram had been a young man with a large family, the promise would be unremarkable. To an old, childless man, it can only be God.

Notice the image, too - dust of the earth. Abram was standing on the very ground he had just given away to Lot. God takes the dirt under his feet and says, "That's how many your descendants will be." God turns what looks like leftovers into a picture of abundance.

Where has your life run out of possibility? Paul says of this very promise that Abram was "fully persuaded that God had power to do what he had promised" (Rom 4:21), and that God "gives life to the dead and calls into being things that were not" (Rom 4:17). Your impossibility is not an obstacle to God - it is the very stage on which He loves to work.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where does your situation seem impossible on human terms?
- Do you believe God has power to do what He has promised?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You make promises that only You can keep, and You work where I have run out of possibility. Strengthen my faith to be fully persuaded that You can do what You have promised.
Amen.
